episodes.title: Picking Up Litter
episodes.text: You arrive at the first yard and pull on your gloves. You walk the lawn with a bag and pick up cups, sticks, and loose trash. You haul the full bag to the truck before any mowing starts.

episodes.title: Raking The Same Beds
episodes.text: You grab your rake and work the same bed edges you did yesterday. You pull leaves and clippings into piles and bag them. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Trimming Beside Someone
episodes.text: You and a coworker stand on opposite sides of the same hedge with hand shears. You work down the row together, keeping your cuts even.

choice.prompt: Your coworker is falling behind on their side of the hedge. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and wait
options.outcome: You stop cutting and hold your shears. Your coworker catches up and the hedge stays even.

options.label: Keep trimming ahead
options.outcome: You keep cutting your side. You finish your stretch and then help pick up the cut branches.

chat.text: Hey, my side is getting higher than yours.
Want to pause so I can catch up?

episodes.title: Watering Dry Spots
episodes.text: You drag the hose to the brown patch by the fence. You spray water slow and even over the grass and around the tree roots. You watch the soil darken as it soaks in.

trial.title: Order the watering steps
items: Spray water evenly over the grass
Drag the hose to the dry lawn edge
Turn on the hose at the spigot
Shut off the hose and drain it
trial.explain: You turn on the water, bring it where it is needed, water, then shut it off.

episodes.title: Mower Hits Debris
episodes.text: You are pushing the mower across the back lawn when it rattles and stops. You see a half-buried bottle caught under the deck. You shut the mower off and step back.

choice.prompt: The mower is clogged on litter. What do you do first?

options.label: Clear it after shutoff
options.outcome: You keep the mower off and pull the bottle out with your hand tool. You restart and the blade spins clear.

options.label: Tip it to look
options.outcome: You leave it off and wait for help to lift it safely. You clear the litter together before you mow on.

episodes.title: Last Pass Mowing
episodes.text: You walk back to the mower for the final strips of the day. You push steady lines up and down the lawn. You park the mower and shake out the grass bag.

episodes.title: Setting Up Clean
episodes.text: You arrive early and pull on gloves. You wipe down the table and chairs. You sterilize the equipment and lay out fresh towels.

episodes.title: First Morning Cleanse
episodes.text: You greet your first client and settle her in the chair. You wash her skin gently with water and a mild cream. You pat it dry and check that it feels clean.

trial.title: Answer about washing
trial.says: How should I wash my skin at home after this?
options: Wash gently with water and a mild cream, pat dry, then follow the simple care steps I show you.
Scrub it hard with hot water so it stays really clean.
Just leave it alone and do not wash it at all this week.
trial.explain: Gentle cleansing and simple aftercare keeps the skin clean without irritation.

episodes.title: Picking Right Products
episodes.text: You look closely at your next client's skin in the bright light. You compare a few mild lotions and shades on a small patch. You think about which will suit her skin and look most natural.

choice.prompt: Two lotions look okay, but one matches her skin a little better. What do you do?

options.label: Use the closer match and explain why
options.outcome: You apply the closer match and tell her why you picked it. She nods and you note her preference for next time.

options.label: Ask her to choose between the two
options.outcome: You hold both up and let her compare in the mirror. She picks one and you write down what she liked.

options.label: Skip the product and move on
options.outcome: You move on without applying anything. Her skin looks a little dry and you make a note to revisit it later.

episodes.title: Midday Wipe Down
episodes.text: You go back to the same sink with the same spray. You sterilize the same equipment and wipe the same counters. It is the same as yesterday and will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Lotion Left Behind
episodes.text: You start to cleanse and find a thick patch of lotion still on the client's skin.

choice.prompt: The skin is not clean enough to continue. What do you do?

options.label: Stop and fully re-cleanse the area
options.outcome: You wash again with water and cream until the residue is gone. The appointment runs a few minutes long.

options.label: Do a quick wipe and continue
options.outcome: You wipe once and move on. A thin film remains and you have to work around it.

chat.text: Oh sorry, I put that on this morning.
Is that going to be a problem?

episodes.title: Writing Day Notes
episodes.text: You sit down at the desk with today's cards. You write down each client's needs and what service you gave. You file the notes so tomorrow starts clear.

episodes.title: Wiping Down Stations
episodes.text: You arrive early and unlock the small studio. You spray and wipe the bed, tray, and tools. You line up fresh brushes the same way as yesterday. Tomorrow you will do it all again.

episodes.title: First Skin Cleanse
episodes.text: You greet your first client and seat her at your station. You dampen cotton pads and gently cleanse the skin around her brows. You rinse and pat the skin dry before you start.

episodes.title: Picking The Shade
episodes.text: You study her brows under the bright lamp. You hold up two tints to compare against her skin.

choice.prompt: She waits while you decide which tint to use on her brows.

options.label: Use the softer brown
options.outcome: You mix and apply the softer brown. She looks in the mirror and nods.

options.label: Use the dark brown
options.outcome: You apply the dark brown. It looks heavier than she wanted, and you note it down.

options.label: Ask her to pick alone
options.outcome: You step back and let her choose without guidance. She hesitates and picks one at random.

chat.text: Will dark brown be too harsh for me?
I don't want them to look painted on.
What do you think would look better?

episodes.title: Teaching Gentle Cleaning
episodes.text: You hand her the mirror after the service. You show her how to wash around the brows with water. You point out how much lotion to use and when.

trial.title: Answer about washing
trial.says: How should I wash my face tonight without ruining these?
options: Just scrub hard with hot water, they will hold.
Use a gentle wash with water around the area and pat dry, with only a light lotion.
Skip washing your face for a week.
trial.explain: Gentle washing with water and light care protects the skin and the work.

episodes.title: Skin Looks Red
episodes.text: You start to cleanse your afternoon client's brow skin. You notice red patches along the brow line. The skin feels tender when you touch it with the damp pad.

choice.prompt: Her skin is getting redder as you wipe. You have to decide what to do right now.

options.label: Stop and rinse gently
options.outcome: You stop wiping and rinse with plain water. You tell her to wait before any tint.

options.label: Keep cleansing the same way
options.outcome: You keep wiping over the red areas. She winces and the redness spreads.

episodes.title: Logging Client Notes
episodes.text: You sit down at the desk at the end of the day. You open her card and write down the tint you used. You note what she liked for next time.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Laundromat Owner — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Focused work time — the skilled part of the day, where doing it well is the whole point. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Litter Walk
episodes.text: You arrive at the first yard with your work gloves on. You walk the lawn slowly with a trash bag. You gather bottles and fallen branches and lift them out of the grass.

episodes.title: Mowing Lanes
episodes.text: You sit down on the mower and start your straight passes. You go up and back across the same flat lawn. It is the same cut as yesterday, and the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Shaping the Hedge
episodes.text: You stand by the tall hedge with your shears in hand. You prune the uneven shrubs back into shape. You trim small cuts and let the clippings fall at your feet.

trial.title: Spot What Needs Trimming
trial.scenario: You step back to check the hedge you just trimmed. Most of it looks even, but one thick branch sticks out past the rest.
options: The long branch sticking out past the line
A short even section in the middle
A clean section you already trimmed
trial.explain: You always take the sticking-out branch first to keep the line even.

episodes.title: Raking With Questions
episodes.text: You are in the side bed with your rake when the homeowner comes out to watch.

choice.prompt: The client wants the leaves under the shrubs now, but you are halfway through the open bed. What do you do?

options.label: Finish this row, then rake under the shrubs
options.outcome: You finish your pass, then reach your rake under the shrubs and pull the leaves out. The whole bed looks clear.

options.label: Stop and reach under the shrubs now
options.outcome: You step over and pull the packed leaves from under the shrubs. You come back to finish the open bed after.

chat.text: Can you get those leaves from under the shrubs too?
I was using a rake but I could not reach back there.

episodes.title: Mower Stalls Out
episodes.text: You are riding the mower over thick wet grass. The blades clog and the mower cuts out. You sit still in the sudden quiet with half the lawn left.

choice.prompt: The mower is clogged and shut down in the middle of the lawn. What do you do first?

options.label: Turn it fully off, then clear the clog by hand
options.outcome: You switch it off, wait, and pull the wet grass free from the deck. The blades turn clear again and you restart.

options.label: Try to restart it right away
options.outcome: You turn the key and the motor strains but stays clogged. You still have to shut it down and clear it.

episodes.title: Evening Watering
episodes.text: You pull the hose to the dry corner of the lawn. You set the portable sprinkler down and turn the water on. You watch the trees and new plants drink it in.

episodes.title: Morning Returns Bin
episodes.text: You arrive and roll the overnight returns bin to the desk. You scan each book back in and stack it for shelving. You check out holds for the patrons waiting at the counter.

episodes.title: Showing the Catalog Search
episodes.text: You sit down with a patron at the public computer to show a basic database search.

choice.prompt: The patron hesitates over the keyboard and looks to you. What do you do next?

options.label: Guide them through one search together
options.outcome: You talk them through one search and they practice clicking through the results. You stay nearby while they try a second one alone.

options.label: Let them practice alone for now
options.outcome: You step back to the desk and check on them in a few minutes. They work slowly and ask you to repeat the steps.

chat.text: I need to find books on this topic but I don't know where to click.
Show them the search box step by step?
Can you stay while I try it once myself?

episodes.title: Answering a Reference Question
episodes.text: You sit at the reference desk with a patron's written question. You open standard reference sources and the internet to check facts. You print the answer and hand it over.

trial.title: Helping with respect
trial.says: Can you help me find a reliable answer to this reference question?
options: I don't do lookups, try guessing online.
Yes, tell me your question and we will search the reference sources together.
Come back tomorrow when it is quieter.
trial.explain: You search standard reference materials together to answer the question.

episodes.title: Wrong Record Blocks Checkout
episodes.text: You try to check out a book and the record shows the wrong copy. You see a cataloging error holding up the line. You open the circulation record to compare it.

choice.prompt: The line is waiting and the record is wrong. What do you fix first?

options.label: Correct the catalog record now
options.outcome: You fix the error in the record and check the book out. The line moves again after a short wait.

options.label: Set it aside and check out the rest
options.outcome: You set the book aside and keep the line moving. You correct the record after the rush and call the patron back.

episodes.title: Stamping the Same Pile
episodes.text: You sit with the circulation log and update the same counts as yesterday. You initial each line and file it. Same pile tomorrow.

episodes.title: Choosing New Books
episodes.text: You sit with book reviews, a catalog, and the current holdings list. You compare what the library already has with faculty requests. You mark a few print and electronic titles to order.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Life Coach — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: Checking Gear Again
episodes.text: You walk around the truck and check your equipment. You look at the same straps, hooks, and tools you checked yesterday. You sign off and put everything back where it always goes.

episodes.title: Drive to Job Site
episodes.text: You climb into the work truck loaded with tools and materials. You drive out to today's job site across town. You park where the crew lead tells you and shut off the engine.

episodes.title: Setting Up Barriers
episodes.text: You unload cones and barriers to close off the work area under the pole. A neighbor walks up wanting to cut through to get to his driveway. You have to decide what to do right now.

choice.prompt: He asks to walk right under the work area. What do you do?

options.label: Hold him back and show the safe way around
options.outcome: He sighs but walks around the cones. You keep the area clear while the crew works.

options.label: Let him hurry through before work starts
options.outcome: He walks under the wires as you watch. You still have to clear the area before anyone can start work.

episodes.title: Up in the Bucket
episodes.text: You climb into the truck bucket and clip in. You rise up to the crossarm to reach the equipment. You look close at the wires and hardware in front of you.

trial.title: Get into work position
items: Raise the bucket up to the equipment
Park the truck and set it stable by the pole
Do the repair work on the equipment
Clip in and get into the bucket
trial.explain: You park and stabilize first, then get in and go up before you touch anything.

episodes.title: Fallen Wire Call
episodes.text: You arrive where a line is down across the road.

choice.prompt: The fallen line is sparking near the curb. What do you do first?

options.label: Open the switch and attach grounds to kill the hazard
options.outcome: The line goes dead and your grounds hold it safe. You can now get close to start the repair.

options.label: Walk in closer to get a better look first
options.outcome: You step toward a live wire on the wet ground. Your crew shouts for you to stop and back out.

chat.text: That line is still live. Stay back.
Open the switch and get your grounds on first.
Barriers are up. Road is blocked both ways.

episodes.title: Fixing the Transformer
episodes.text: You sit in the bucket at the pole with the new parts beside you. You swap out the damaged cable and switch on the transformer. You check the connections hold tight before you come down.

episodes.title: First Meeting
episodes.text: You sit down with a new applicant at your desk. You ask about income, debts, and what they want to borrow for. You write down their answers for the loan application.

choice.prompt: The applicant did not bring proof of income. What do you do now?

options.label: Pause and list what to bring back
options.outcome: You stop the application and give them a short list. They leave to gather the missing papers.

options.label: Continue with what you have
options.outcome: You fill in what you can and note what is missing. The file stays open until the proof arrives.

episodes.title: Explaining Options
episodes.text: You sit with a customer who is unsure which loan fits. You explain the different loan types and credit options in plain terms. You go over the terms so they know the costs.

episodes.title: Checking the Numbers
episodes.text: You pull up an applicant's credit report and pay records. You compare income and debts against the property value. You note whether the loan looks feasible.

trial.title: Spot the problem
trial.scenario: You review a file. Income covers the payment. The property evaluation came in much lower than the loan amount. The credit report shows on-time payments.
options: Low property value
On-time payments
Steady income
trial.explain: The low property value makes the loan unsafe to approve as written.

episodes.title: Questions About Process
episodes.text: A returning applicant stops by with questions about the next steps.

chat.text: How long does the application take from here?
You answer what happens next in the process.
And what do you need from me now?

episodes.title: Over the Limit
episodes.text: You review a loan request that is larger than you can approve. The numbers are complete but the amount is outside your limit. You cannot sign it yourself today.

choice.prompt: The loan is over your approval limit. What do you do?

options.label: Approve it within your limit only
options.outcome: You approve a smaller amount you are allowed to sign. The applicant decides whether to accept it.

options.label: Refer it to management
options.outcome: You send the full request up to management for review. The applicant waits for their decision.

options.label: Deny it outright
options.outcome: You close the request without a referral. The applicant must start over if they want a smaller loan.

episodes.title: Sending for Review
episodes.text: You sit and submit today's finished applications to the credit analysts. You attach each form the same way as yesterday. Tomorrow you will do the same stack again.

episodes.title: Cutting Morning Keys
episodes.text: You arrive at the shop bench and switch on the key cutting machine. You clamp in the customer's worn key and a blank and copy the cuts.

trial.title: Copy a key
items: Run the cutter along the original to shape the blank
Test the new key in the lock
Pick a matching blank key
Clamp the original and blank in the machine
trial.explain: You pick the blank and clamp both keys before you cut and test.

episodes.title: Locked Out Front Door
episodes.text: You kneel at a front door with no key. The renter stands behind you waiting.

choice.prompt: The pick is tight in the cylinder and will not turn. What do you do now?

options.label: Ease off and keep picking
options.outcome: You lighten your touch and work the pins slowly. The cylinder turns after a few more minutes.

options.label: Stop and try a different pick
options.outcome: You pull out and swap to another pick. You start again on the cylinder from the beginning.

chat.text: I left my keys inside this morning.
Can you get it open without breaking it?
Take your time, I am late but I get it.

episodes.title: Changing Lock Tumblers
episodes.text: You sit at the bench with a lock taken apart. You place new tumblers inside to change the combination. You fit them in and check that the old key no longer turns.

episodes.title: More Duplicate Keys
episodes.text: You are back at the cutting machine after lunch. You cut the same kind of duplicates as yesterday. You stack them up and do it again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Drilling The Stuck Safe
episodes.text: You stand in front of a safe that will not open. You set up to open the safe lock by drilling. Metal dust falls as you drill into the lock body.

choice.prompt: The drill breaks through but the safe stays shut. What do you do?

options.label: Stop drilling and check the hole
options.outcome: You stop the drill and clear the hole. You see what is still holding and drill a little more.

options.label: Keep drilling deeper
options.outcome: You keep the drill running a bit longer. You punch through more metal and then stop to check.

episodes.title: Cutting Code Key
episodes.text: You sit down with a code for a lost key. You set the code key machine by the numbers. You cut a new key from the code.

episodes.title: Reading Today's Orders
episodes.text: You arrive in the crew room and sit down with the paperwork. You read through the train orders and the signals for your run. You check the railroad rules that cover how you will operate today.

trial.title: Starting the locomotive
items: Open the throttle to move the locomotive
Receive the starting signal from the conductor
Drive the locomotive forward
Release the air brakes
trial.explain: You wait for the signal first, then release the brakes and use the throttle to move.

episodes.title: Radio Check With Conductor
episodes.text: You pick up the radiophone in the cab for the morning check. You wait for the conductor and control to come on.

chat.text: Engineer, are you ready for the stop list?
Control here. One oncoming train ahead, expect a short wait.
Copy that. I will call out our stops as we go.

episodes.title: Watching the Gauges
episodes.text: You sit and watch the gauges for speed and air pressure. You glance at amperage and battery charge, then back to speed. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Pulling Out of Yard
episodes.text: You watch for the conductor and get the starting signal. You put your hand on the throttle and the air brake. You ease the diesel-electric locomotive forward out of the yard.

choice.prompt: The starting signal is hard to see. What do you do?

options.label: Hold the brakes and ask the conductor to repeat the signal
options.outcome: You stay stopped and the conductor repeats the signal clearly. You start moving a minute later.

options.label: Ease open the throttle and start rolling slowly
options.outcome: You start to move without a clear signal and have to stop hard. The conductor calls you to wait.

episodes.title: Something On The Tracks
episodes.text: You keep your eyes on the rails ahead. You see a shape on the track that should not be there. You reach toward the brake as the distance closes.

choice.prompt: There is an obstruction on the track ahead. What do you do first?

options.label: Apply the air brakes right away
options.outcome: The train slows fast and stops short of the object. You sit still and report what you see.

options.label: Call control on the radiophone first
options.outcome: You get control on the radio while still moving. You then brake hard and stop closer than you want.

options.label: Sound the horn and keep watching
options.outcome: You sound the horn but keep rolling toward the object. You have to brake hard at the last moment.

episodes.title: Reporting the Delay
episodes.text: You are stopped past schedule and pick up the radiophone. You confer with the conductor about the delay at your stop. You give control your position and ask about oncoming trains.

episodes.title: Morning Customer Messages
episodes.text: You arrive and open your inbox. You read overnight notes from two customers about late arrivals. You list what each one says they need today.

episodes.title: Quick Check-in Call
episodes.text: You call the warehouse contact to keep the relationship steady. You ask what is working and what is not.

choice.prompt: The contact is waiting for your response on the late drop. What do you do?

options.label: Promise to look into the morning slot today
options.outcome: You note the request and start checking what can change for tomorrow morning.

options.label: Ask what a good morning delivery looks like
options.outcome: The contact describes the time window and you write it down to act on.

chat.text: Morning. Yesterday’s drop was late again.
We need the morning slot to actually hold.

episodes.title: Same Status Update
episodes.text: You sit down to log the same subcontractor updates you log every day. You copy the notes into the same sheet. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Drafting Cost Proposal
episodes.text: You sit at your desk after lunch. You pull together a proposal with the estimate paperwork. You check each line before you save the draft.

episodes.title: Subcontractor Missed Spec
episodes.text: You review a subcontractor proposal and see it misses the performance spec. You need to act as the link between them and your company.

choice.prompt: The subcontractor proposal does not meet the spec. What do you do first?

options.label: Send it back with the spec points marked
options.outcome: You mark what misses the spec and ask for a revised proposal.

options.label: Set up a quick call between both sides
options.outcome: You get everyone on the phone and walk through the spec gap together.

options.label: Hold it and check with your team first
options.outcome: You pause the proposal and confirm what your company will accept.

episodes.title: Reviewing Weekly Performance
episodes.text: You sit with the customer to review this week’s performance. You compare what happened against the targets and service agreement.

trial.title: Find what needs attention
trial.scenario: You review deliveries against the service agreement. Most runs met the target time. One lane missed the target twice and has no backup plan.
options: The lane that missed target twice
A lane that met its target
The cover page of the report
trial.explain: The repeated miss against the agreement needs attention first.

episodes.title: Morning Vitals Round
episodes.text: You arrive on the floor and pick up the vitals cart. You move from bed to bed taking temperature, blood pressure, pulse, and respiration. You write each number down, same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Answering the Call
episodes.text: You hear the call light ring and step into the room.

choice.prompt: The patient needs help now. What do you do first?

options.label: Help them to the bathroom with support
options.outcome: You steady them and walk with them to the bathroom. You stay close so they do not fall.

options.label: Check their leg and ask about the pain first
options.outcome: You look at the leg and ask where it hurts and how bad it feels. You then decide if they can stand safely.

options.label: Tell them you will come back in a few minutes
options.outcome: You finish another task and return to the room. The light is still on and they are still waiting.

chat.text: Can you help me? I need to use the bathroom and my leg hurts.
I feel a little shaky when I stand up.

episodes.title: Changing a Dressing
episodes.text: You sit down beside the bed with clean supplies. You take off the old dressing and look at the skin. You clean the area and put on a fresh dressing.

episodes.title: Giving Midday Meds
episodes.text: You check the medication list for the afternoon. You bring the prescribed pills to the bedside and watch the patient take them. You note the time and amount on the chart.

trial.title: Give the right meds
items: Write down the time and amount on the chart
Give the prescribed pills to the patient
Check the prescription on the chart
Check the patient's wristband
trial.explain: You check what is ordered and who the patient is before you give anything.

episodes.title: Rash After Medication
episodes.text: You come back to check and see a new red rash on the arms. You ask how they feel and take temperature and blood pressure. You know this could be a bad reaction to the medication.

choice.prompt: You see a possible reaction to medication. What do you do?

options.label: Stay with them and call the nurse right away
options.outcome: You stay in the room and report the rash and vitals. Help comes to decide what to do next.

options.label: Chart the rash and keep watching alone
options.outcome: You write down what you see and keep checking. No one else knows about the change yet.

episodes.title: Charting the Day
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and open the charts. You add the vital signs, medication times, and wound care notes. You write down the rash and who you told about it.

episodes.title: Matching Buyer List
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open the buyer notes. You check their needs and financial limits. You pull together a short list of properties that fit.

episodes.title: Drafting Contract Papers
episodes.text: You sit down to prepare the representation contract and purchase agreement. You fill in names, terms, and dates. You read it through for errors before printing.

episodes.title: Showing the Offer
episodes.text: You meet the sellers at the kitchen table to present the purchase offer.

choice.prompt: The sellers ask what you think of the offer. How do you present it?

options.label: Read each term plainly
options.outcome: You read the price and conditions line by line. They ask questions and take the papers to think.

options.label: Highlight the strong parts first
options.outcome: You point out the clean closing date and down payment. They still ask to hear the rest of the terms.

chat.text: Walk us through what they offered.
Is this what we asked for?

episodes.title: Afternoon Status Checks
episodes.text: You sit with your list and call about open purchase agreements. You check the same boxes as yesterday. You log the answers and do it again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Stuck Negotiation Call
episodes.text: You get calls from both buyer and seller over one repair term. Neither side will move. You need to carry a response back now.

choice.prompt: Both sides are waiting on this term. What do you do next?

options.label: Carry the latest counter over
options.outcome: You pass the seller's counter to the buyer word for word. The buyer asks for an hour to decide.

options.label: Ask for one small move
options.outcome: You ask each side if they can shift a little on the date. They both pause and say they will think about it.

options.label: Pause until tomorrow
options.outcome: You tell both sides you will pick this up in the morning. The file sits still overnight.

episodes.title: Closing Terms Review
episodes.text: You sit down to confer on a file closing soon. You call the lender, inspector, and escrow company. You check that the purchase terms will be met before the date.

trial.title: What Needs Attention First
trial.scenario: You check a file closing this week. The lender papers are ready and the inspection is done. The escrow company says one closing condition is still not met.
options: The open escrow condition
The finished inspection
The ready lender papers
trial.explain: You handle the unmet condition first so the closing can stay on track.

episodes.title: Reading Script Notes
episodes.text: You arrive early and sit down with today's script pages. You mark where a scene change affects how each character should look.

episodes.title: First Face On
episodes.text: The first actor sits in your chair before filming starts.

choice.prompt: The actor's skin looks a little different than yesterday. What do you do?

options.label: Adjust the makeup to match yesterday's look
options.outcome: You blend carefully and the face matches the reference again.

options.label: Keep going with the usual routine
options.outcome: You finish, but the difference shows a little on camera.

chat.text: I was out in the sun yesterday. Will that matter?
You check the reference photo from yesterday.

episodes.title: Same Look Again
episodes.text: You do the second actor's look exactly like yesterday. Same colors. Same placement. Same as tomorrow.

episodes.title: Washing Brushes Out
episodes.text: You bring your used brushes to the sink between scenes. You wash and lay them out to dry.

trial.title: Check the brushes
trial.scenario: You line up your clean brushes to dry. Two look clean and dry. One still holds old color deep near the handle.
options: Wash again the brush still holding color
Put all the brushes away now
Throw away the clean brushes
trial.explain: A brush holding old color can change the next face.

episodes.title: Watching For Touch-Ups
episodes.text: You stand near the set and watch the monitor. You check that the makeup still looks steady take to take.

episodes.title: Lights Suddenly Shift
episodes.text: The lighting changes for the next setup. The makeup that looked right now looks too pale.

choice.prompt: They are about to roll again. What do you do?

options.label: Step in fast and adjust the makeup now
options.outcome: You even out the tone quickly and filming starts on time.

options.label: Wait and fix it after this take
options.outcome: You watch the take, then adjust before the next one.

options.label: Leave it and hope it reads fine
options.outcome: The difference stays visible through the take.

episodes.title: Drafting Morning Questions
episodes.text: You open the draft survey on buying habits. You read each question slowly to catch confusing wording. You mark where people might stop and quit. You lay out the steps to fix it.

trial.title: Put Survey Steps In Order
items: Send the final questionnaire to the full list
Test the draft questions with a small group
Write the first draft of the survey questions
Fix the confusing questions you found in the test
trial.explain: You write first, test small, fix, then send wide.

episodes.title: Checking Same Responses
episodes.text: You sit with new responses on customer age and buying habits. You check each row and flag the incomplete ones. It is the same file as yesterday, and the same checks tomorrow.

episodes.title: Talking Through Early Answers
episodes.text: You join a video call with two marketing staff to go over early consumer opinions.

choice.prompt: They want a survey question that pushes for a positive answer. What do you do?

options.label: Keep the question neutral
options.outcome: You keep the wording neutral. The answers stay usable and the marketers wait a bit longer for a clear read.

options.label: Add their version as well
options.outcome: You add their wording as a separate test question. You flag it as leading so it does not mix with the main results.

chat.text: We are seeing good comments on price, but not on the new pack. Can we ask about it more directly?
What if we ask: Don't you like the new pack better?

episodes.title: Turning Numbers Into Charts
episodes.text: You turn the cleaned age and demand table into a simple bar chart. You look for where interest drops off. You write one plain paragraph under it saying what changed.

episodes.title: Missing Satisfaction Answers
episodes.text: You open the customer satisfaction file and half the morning answers are missing.

choice.prompt: The satisfaction data is incomplete and someone wants it now. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and check the collection first
options.outcome: You hold the numbers back and check the survey link and returns. You find the gap and note it before anyone uses the data.

options.label: Share what you have with a warning
options.outcome: You send the partial satisfaction count with a clear note about what is missing. They wait for the full count before deciding.

chat.text: The satisfaction numbers look thin for today. Are we still good to share them?
Can you tell me what is safe to use right now?

episodes.title: Writing Up Findings
episodes.text: You sit down to finish the report of findings. You paste in the charts and write what they mean in plain words. You save the file for review.

episodes.title: Morning First Meeting
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with new clients for a first talk. You ask about their history and listen to how they describe the problem. You watch how they speak to each other in the room.

episodes.title: Naming What Happened
episodes.text: You sit with a teenager who goes quiet after a fight at home. You ask simple questions and give time to answer.

choice.prompt: He stops talking and looks away. Do you press on or stay with what he just said?

options.label: Stay with what he said
options.outcome: You ask what he felt right before he shut down. He names anger and shame and you talk through both.

options.label: Ask about behavior first
options.outcome: You ask what he did after he shut down. He lists what happened and you link it back to the feeling.

chat.text: I don't know. I just shut down.
Then I said things I didn't mean.

episodes.title: Building the Plan
episodes.text: You sit alone and look over your notes on a family. You name the relationship problem and the pattern that keeps repeating. You write an individualized treatment plan to address them.

trial.title: Order the plan steps
items: Put the plan into action with the family
Name the destructive pattern you see
Write an individualized treatment plan
Learn about the family relationship problem
trial.explain: You learn the problem first, then plan, then use the plan.

episodes.title: Afternoon Skills Practice
episodes.text: You sit with clients and walk through the same calm-speaking exercise as yesterday. You encourage them to use the steps to handle disagreement in a constructive way. Same worksheet, same practice, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Voices Rise Fast
episodes.text: You sit between parents as their talk turns sharp and loud. You step in and encourage them to use words that do not attack. You remind them of the constructive strategy they practiced.

choice.prompt: Both start talking at once and no one listens. What do you do next?

options.label: Pause and reset the talk
options.outcome: You stop the talk and have them speak one at a time. The volume drops and they finish the session safely.

options.label: Coach one skill right now
options.outcome: You pick one constructive sentence and have each repeat it. They use the skill to get through the next few minutes.

options.label: End the exercise early
options.outcome: You close the exercise and move to calm breathing. You agree to return to the topic next time.

episodes.title: Closing Case Notes
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and open today's case files. You add activities, progress notes, and evaluations for each session. You file recommendations so the record is complete.

episodes.title: Morning Health Talk
episodes.text: You sit down with your first client before the table is ready. You ask about her medical history and where she feels stress or pain. You listen to decide how massage will help her today.

choice.prompt: She mentions an old back injury and new neck stress from work. How do you use this to guide today?

options.label: Focus today on the neck stress
options.outcome: You note the back injury for later and plan the session around her neck and shoulders.

options.label: Ask one more question about the back
options.outcome: She explains the old injury aches when pressed hard, so you mark gentle pressure for that area.

episodes.title: Hands On Shoulders
episodes.text: You stand at the table and start the session. You massage and knead the muscles in her neck and shoulders. You keep your pressure steady for wellness maintenance.

episodes.title: Pressure On Points
episodes.text: Your next client asks for help with tight hands and feet. You use your fingers and thumbs to press specific points. You hold, release, and move to the next point.

episodes.title: Wiping Down Room
episodes.text: You wipe down the table and headrest with sanitizer. You restock clean towels and check the oil bottles. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Planning Next Visits
episodes.text: You sit with your afternoon client after his session. You look over his pain notes and what helped today. You explain which types of massage you suggest for the next visits.

trial.title: Pick Treatment Focus
trial.scenario: He has ongoing low-back pain from an injury and also wants general wellness maintenance. You must propose what the next plan focuses on first.
options: Sanitizing the massage equipment
Treating the low-back injury
Restocking towels and oil
trial.explain: The injury treatment comes first in the proposed plan.

episodes.title: Sharp Pain Stops You
episodes.text: You are massaging a client's calf for an old injury when she tenses up.

choice.prompt: She is in pain under your hands. What do you do right now?

options.label: Stop and check the pain
options.outcome: You lift your hands and ask where it hurts and how it feels. You adjust to gentle pressure around the spot.

options.label: Keep kneading through it
options.outcome: You keep working the muscle but she stays tense. You finish the area quickly and move on.

chat.text: Ouch, that spot really hurts right now.
Is that normal for this treatment?

episodes.title: Checking Old Stock
episodes.text: You arrive and unlock the cooler. You check dates and look closely at vegetables and cooked trays. You move the older items forward and place the new ones behind them.

episodes.title: Setting Oven Heat
episodes.text: You stand by the ovens before the first big cook. You turn the dials and watch the gauges climb. You steady the heat so the food will cook through safely.

trial.title: Plating in order
items: Serve food to waiters
Garnish the plates
Portion the food
Arrange food on the plates
trial.explain: You portion first, then arrange, garnish, and serve last.

episodes.title: Wiping Same Counters
episodes.text: You wipe the same work surfaces and equipment again. You rinse the cloth, wipe, and check the serving area. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Handing Up Lunch
episodes.text: You stand at the pass with portioned trays ready. A waiter stops beside you for the next order.

choice.prompt: One plate is missing garnish and the waiter is waiting. What do you do?

options.label: Add garnish quickly, then hand it over
options.outcome: You add the garnish and hand the tray over. He leaves with the full order a minute later.

options.label: Hand it over as is
options.outcome: You hand the plate over without garnish. The order goes out incomplete.

chat.text: Is tray twelve ready to go?
Does it have the garnish on top?
I can take it now if it is set.

episodes.title: Oven Running Hot
episodes.text: You smell the batch browning too fast. You look and the oven gauge reads higher than you set. You open the door and see the tops darkening.

choice.prompt: The oven is too hot for this batch. What do you do first?

options.label: Turn the heat down and check the food temp
options.outcome: You lower the heat and check the centers. You pull what is done and leave the rest to finish slower.

options.label: Leave the heat and take the trays out early
options.outcome: You pull the trays early. The tops are dark and the centers are still cool.

options.label: Move the trays to a cooler oven
options.outcome: You shift the trays to a steady oven. They finish cooking at a safe temperature.

episodes.title: Seasoning Final Batch
episodes.text: You taste the broth from the last pot. You add salt and stir, then taste again. You set the trays in to cook through.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Mechanical Engineer — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Draft On Desk
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down with yesterday's draft decision. You read it again against the regulation in front of you. You mark two lines where the wording does not match the law.

episodes.title: Hearing Opens
episodes.text: You call the hearing to order and ask both sides to speak. You ask for the documents that support each claim. You listen and write down what each person says happened.

episodes.title: Objection Over Paper
episodes.text: You pause the hearing when one side objects to a letter being used. You look at the letter and listen to both reasons. You have to rule now so the hearing can go on.

choice.prompt: The letter was brought late and one side says it should not count. Do you let it in?

options.label: Let the letter in
options.outcome: You note the late arrival on the record and let the hearing continue with the letter included.

options.label: Keep the letter out
options.outcome: You set the letter aside and tell both sides to continue with the evidence already accepted.

episodes.title: Same Files Again
episodes.text: You sit with the same law book and the same kind of claim file. You check facts against the same precedents line by line. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Talking Through Liability
episodes.text: You bring both sides back in to close the question of who owes what.

choice.prompt: The evidence shows shared fault but not equal shares. How do you set liability?

options.label: Split it evenly
options.outcome: You record equal liability for both sides and explain how the evidence supports a shared split.

options.label: Put more on one side
options.outcome: You record a larger share for one side and point to the receipts and testimony behind it.

options.label: Hold for more proof
options.outcome: You ask for the missing receipts by tomorrow before you set the final shares.

chat.text: We have receipts for half the repair cost. That should count for something.
We did not agree to that work. Why should we pay for all of it?
So who decides how much is fair here?

episodes.title: Writing The Decision
episodes.text: You sit down to write the opinion for today's case. You set the hearing notes beside the law. You write what you found and what you decided.

trial.title: Put the decision in order
items: Write the opinion in clear terms
Compare the evidence to the law
Decide how far liability goes
Review the hearing notes
trial.explain: You review notes first, then apply the law, then decide liability, then write it down.

episodes.title: Straightening Exam Rooms
episodes.text: You arrive early and walk the row of exam rooms. You wipe the tables and straighten the chairs the same as yesterday. You replace the paper and check each room is neat and clean. It will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: First Patient Check-In
episodes.text: You call in the first patient and bring them back to the exam area. You reach for the cuff and the scale to start vitals.

choice.prompt: The patient looks uneasy as you start measuring vitals and asking history. What do you do first?

options.label: Measure vitals first, then ask history
options.outcome: You take blood pressure, weight, and height first. The patient settles a little while you then ask about medical information.

options.label: Ask history first, then measure vitals
options.outcome: You sit down and interview for medical information first. You then stand to measure weight, height, and vital signs.

chat.text: I get nervous having all this measured.
Do you need my full history again today?

episodes.title: Charting Morning Visits
episodes.text: You sit down at the desk with the morning charts. You enter each patient's medical history and vital statistics. You add the test results to the medical records.

episodes.title: Explaining Aftercare Clearly
episodes.text: You walk back in with the discharge sheet for a patient. You sit at eye level to go over the next steps.

chat.text: So what did the doctor say about the pills and food?
I did not catch all of those instructions.
They are ready to check out when you are done.

episodes.title: Spill in the Hallway
episodes.text: You find a bag of contaminated supplies has tipped in the hall. Used gauze and instruments are near the clean cart. You need to clear it safely right now.

choice.prompt: The contaminated supplies are on the floor next to clean items. What do you handle first?

options.label: Block the area and dispose of contaminated supplies
options.outcome: You keep people back and place the contaminated supplies in the right container. You then wipe down the area before touching the clean cart.

options.label: Move the clean cart away first
options.outcome: You roll the clean cart clear so it stays clean. You then pick up and dispose of the contaminated supplies safely.

options.label: Call for help and wait by the spill
options.outcome: You stand by the spill to warn others until help comes. You then clean up and dispose of the contaminated supplies together.

episodes.title: Cleaning Steel Tools
episodes.text: You bring the last tray of used instruments to the back. You wash each piece and set them up to sterilize. You throw out the contaminated supplies in the marked bin.

trial.title: Clean Tools in Order
items: Dispose of contaminated supplies in the right bin
Collect the used instruments
Sterilize the cleaned instruments
Wash and clean the instruments
trial.explain: You collect, then wash, then sterilize, then dispose of what is left.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Medical Coder — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Delivery List
episodes.text: You arrive at dispatch and check in in person. You receive today's materials and the names, addresses, and delivery instructions. You listen and sort the stops for hospitals and clinics.

episodes.title: Loading the Van
episodes.text: You stand at the back of your van with the listed goods. You load specimens, records, and medications in the right places. You take extra care with the hazardous goods.

trial.title: Load in the right order
items: Take precautions with the hazardous goods
Check the listed goods for this run
Confirm everything is loaded correctly
Load the goods into the vehicle
trial.explain: You check the list first, then load, protect the hazardous items, and confirm the load.

episodes.title: Same Stops Again
episodes.text: You drive to the next hospital and drop off the lab specimens. You pick up the return records and medications. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Clinic Front Desk
episodes.text: You arrive at the clinic with medications. You meet the staff at the front desk.

choice.prompt: The staff asks you to wait while they count the medications before signing. What do you do?

options.label: Wait for the count and signature
options.outcome: You wait at the desk. You get the signature and head to your next stop a few minutes late.

options.label: Ask to leave them and come back
options.outcome: You ask if you can return after your next drop. You come back later for the signature.

chat.text: Are these our morning meds?
We need them signed in now.
Can you wait while I check the count?

episodes.title: Missing Signature Payment
episodes.text: You bring records to a medical office for pickup. The recipient will not sign and cannot pay right now. You need a signature and to sort out the payment.

choice.prompt: The recipient cannot pay and hesitates to sign. What do you do?

options.label: Arrange for them to pay later
options.outcome: You note the agreement to pay later and get the signature now. You record the payment plan on your log.

options.label: Hold the delivery until sorted
options.outcome: You wait and call dispatch on your radio for instructions. You follow what they tell you to do next.

options.label: Take the items back
options.outcome: You keep the items with you and record no delivery. You bring them back on your next run.

episodes.title: Logging the Day
episodes.text: You sit down with your log at the end of the route. You record what you received and delivered and who signed. You add notes on payments and responses to messages.

episodes.title: Outlining the Scan
episodes.text: You sit down at your workstation and open today's CT scan. You scroll through the slices and trace the outline of the lungs and spinal cord. You save the contours for the planning work ahead.

episodes.title: Shaping the Beams
episodes.text: You open the planning computer with your manuals and guides beside you. You arrange the radiation fields around the target area. You shift one field slightly to reduce exposure to a nearby organ.

episodes.title: Talking Through Shields
episodes.text: You sit with the planning screen open beside your colleague. You point to where the beam passes close to healthy tissue.

choice.prompt: Which beam modifying device do you plan to use first?

options.label: Add a shield to block the healthy tissue
options.outcome: You add the shield in the plan and rerun the display to see the new coverage.

options.label: Add a wedge filter to shape the dose
options.outcome: You add the wedge in the plan and check how the dose shifts across the field.

chat.text: That beam is going straight through a lot of healthy tissue, right?
Do you think a shield or a wedge would help here?
What do you want to try first?

episodes.title: Same Calculations Again
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk and open the dose calculation sheet. You check the same prescribed numbers you checked yesterday. You initial the boxes and move to the next sheet, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Calculating Today's Dose
episodes.text: You pull up the prescription for the afternoon patient. You calculate the amount of radiation per session. You enter the numbers and double-check the math.

trial.title: What Needs Attention First
trial.scenario: You review a new plan. The target area is covered, but one field passes straight through the spinal cord. The wedge filter looks in place.
options: The field hitting the spinal cord
The covered target area
The wedge filter in place
trial.explain: The field hitting a critical organ needs attention first before anything else.

episodes.title: Dose Check Fails
episodes.text: You verify the final dose calculation before sign-off. The total does not match the prescribed dose. You pause the plan and keep the chart open on your screen.

choice.prompt: The verified dose does not match the prescription. What do you do?

options.label: Recalculate the dose yourself now
options.outcome: You work through the calculation again line by line and compare it to the prescription.

options.label: Hold the plan and ask for a second check
options.outcome: You leave the plan on hold and bring the numbers to another checker to review with you.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Medical Laboratory Scientist — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Walk Through
episodes.text: You arrive in steel toes and walk the line with your flashlight. You check the pumps and conveyors for leaks and loose guards. You mark two spots that need attention later.

episodes.title: Grease and Oil
episodes.text: You push the grease cart down the same row as yesterday. You wipe each fitting, pump grease, and check the oil cups. You move to the next motor and do it all again.

episodes.title: Guiding the Load
episodes.text: You stand by the bedplate and raise your hands to the crane operator. The basic assembly unit hangs above you on the hook.

choice.prompt: The unit is coming down a little left of the centerline. What do you do?

options.label: Hold and signal a small move right
options.outcome: You hold the lower and signal right. The operator shifts the load and sets it down on the centerline.

options.label: Let it land and pry it over
options.outcome: You let it land left and push with a pry bar. You spend extra time jacking it back to the centerline.

chat.text: Ready when you are. I have it just above the bedplate.
Tell me which way to go.

episodes.title: Setting the Clearance
episodes.text: You kneel at the machine with your hand tools and feeler gauges. You position the part and work shims under the foot. You snug the nuts and bolts and check the clearance again.

trial.title: Set the clearance
items: Adjust tension on nuts and bolts
Position the part in place
Check clearance with measuring instruments
Insert shims under the part
trial.explain: You position, shim, tighten, then check the gap is correct.

episodes.title: Broken Part Stops Line
episodes.text: You hear a knock and find a cracked part with too much play. You lock out the machine and pull your hand tools. You need to fix the clearance before it runs again.

choice.prompt: The moving part is loose and the spare is on the bench. What do you do first?

options.label: Replace the defective part now
options.outcome: You pull the bad part and fit the new one. You adjust the alignment and the knock goes away.

options.label: Shim and tighten to get by
options.outcome: You adjust the clearances and tighten it up. The machine runs rough and you still need the new part.

episodes.title: Laser Line Check
episodes.text: You set up on the motor and pump with your squares and laser. You read the offset and loosen the feet. You jack the motor over until the faces line up.

episodes.title: Morning Health Check
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and open your laptop. You check the crash logs and server status from overnight. You compare them to the spec limits. Everything is running as it should.

episodes.title: Design Call Together
episodes.text: You join a video call with an engineer and a systems analyst. You ask about project limits and what the app interface needs to handle. You listen as they explain the performance requirements.

choice.prompt: The analyst says one requested feature will not fit the current limits. What do you do?

options.label: Ask what to cut back
options.outcome: You ask which part can be smaller. They agree to a simpler version that fits the limits.

options.label: Keep the design as is
options.outcome: You keep the current design for now. You note the risk and move on to the next item.

episodes.title: Checking User Requests
episodes.text: You open three user requests for offline mode. You check each one against time and cost limits. You mark one large idea as not feasible for this round.

trial.title: Order the test steps
items: Run the test on the build
Write the test steps for the new fix
Note what passed and what failed
Fix issues and run the test again
trial.explain: You write the steps first, then run, record, and fix.

episodes.title: Same System Check
episodes.text: You refresh the same system monitor you checked this morning. You look at the same numbers and log them again. Nothing has changed. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Install Stalls Halfway
episodes.text: You start the planned software install for test users and it stalls halfway. You watch the error notice come up.

choice.prompt: The install is stuck and testers are waiting. What do you do?

options.label: Roll back the install
options.outcome: You roll back to the last working version. Testers can keep working while you check the logs.

options.label: Try the install once more
options.outcome: You run the install step again and watch the logs. It stalls in the same place and you stop it.

chat.text: Install stuck at 50% on my side too
Can you hold it for now so testers are not blocked?
I can stay on to check the logs with you

episodes.title: Updating Test Notes
episodes.text: You open the testing document for today's build. You write down what you tested and what passed. You save the file so the team has the current version.

episodes.title: Morning Lot Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the yard and pull your van beside the loader. You climb in and operate it slow across the lot. You inspect the steering and lift as you drive.

trial.title: Find the fault first
trial.scenario: You operate the loader and inspect it to diagnose the defect. The engine starts fine and the lights work. The lift shudders and drops on the left side.
options: The left lift cylinder is worn
The headlight bulb is old
The seat cover is torn
trial.explain: You check the lift first because that is the defect you found on inspection.

episodes.title: Manual on the Hood
episodes.text: You sit on your bumper and open the operating manual for this loader. You read the blueprint for the lift assembly. You trace the drawing with your finger until it makes sense.

episodes.title: Same Worn Parts
episodes.text: You repair the same kind of worn pins you did yesterday. You replace them one by one with hand tools. Same work, same order, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Explaining the Worn Brake
episodes.text: The site manager walks over while you have the brake parts laid out.

choice.prompt: The brake pads are worn past safe use. He wants a quick patch to keep working. What do you do?

options.label: Replace the worn brake parts now
options.outcome: You replace the damaged parts now. The machine is down for an hour, then it is safe to run.

options.label: Patch it and come back later
options.outcome: You explain you cannot leave bad brakes. You replace the parts now and show him the old ones.

chat.text: Can you just patch it so we can run today?
We really need this machine moving.

episodes.title: Test Fails Twice
episodes.text: You finish the repair and test the loader after assembly. It still does not meet the maker’s spec on the lift. You shut it down and wipe your hands.

choice.prompt: The lift test fails after repair. The customer is waiting. What do you do next?

options.label: Dismantle the lift again to check
options.outcome: You dismantle the assembly with hoists and hand tools. You find the worn seal you missed and fix it.

options.label: Test it once more the same way
options.outcome: You run the same test again. It fails the same way, so you shut it down and open it up.

options.label: Call it good enough for today
options.outcome: You do not sign it off. You keep it parked until the lift passes the spec.

episodes.title: Reassemble and Finish
episodes.text: You lift the heavy housing back with your hoist. You reassemble the equipment with hand tools. You tighten the last bolts and pack up your tools.

episodes.title: Morning Health Check
episodes.text: You arrive and walk the row of pens. You stop at each animal and look at eyes, skin, and how it moves. You note who seems dull or stiff this morning.

trial.title: Spot what needs attention
trial.scenario: You are observing the animals for illness or injury. One is eating normally, one is sleeping quietly, and one is holding one leg up and not putting weight on it.
options: The animal holding its leg up and not bearing weight
The animal eating its breakfast normally
The animal sleeping quietly in the corner
trial.explain: Not bearing weight on a leg is a clear sign of possible injury that needs checking first.

episodes.title: Breakfast Bowls Out
episodes.text: You fill the same bowls with the same feed and water. You work down the schedule line by line. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Mixing Special Meals
episodes.text: You sit down with the feeding instructions and supplement labels. You measure and mix the food, liquid formula, and supplements as written. You set each mix by the right pen.

episodes.title: Something Looks Off
episodes.text: You check the animals again after midday. One that ate this morning now refuses water and looks tired. You watch its breathing and check for other signs.

choice.prompt: The animal refuses water and looks tired — what do you do next?

options.label: Keep watching it closely for now
options.outcome: You stay nearby and recheck it in a little while to see if it worsens or improves.

options.label: Examine it more closely for illness or injury
options.outcome: You look it over carefully for discharge, swelling, or soreness and make notes on what you find.

episodes.title: A Limp and Call
episodes.text: You find one animal limping with a swollen paw. You clean the area and see the swelling is getting worse. You decide it needs more help than you can give here.

choice.prompt: The paw is swollen and the limp is worse — what do you do?

options.label: Give basic first treatment and keep it quiet
options.outcome: You clean the paw, keep the animal still, and watch closely while you arrange next help.

options.label: Contact the veterinarian to secure treatment
options.outcome: You call the veterinarian, describe what you see, and follow their instructions for care.

options.label: Move it back with the others and recheck later
options.outcome: You put it back in its pen and come back soon to see if the swelling or limp changes.

episodes.title: Washing and Disinfecting
episodes.text: You gather the laundry and load the washer. You scrub, disinfect, and organize the pens and equipment. You set everything ready for the morning feed.
